summary: The plan covers all explicit requests: real‑time analysis, pitch, spectrogram, trainer‑style features, plain‑language explanations, and a simple UI. Two aspects remain ambiguous because the request left design choices open: which trainer‑inspired features to include and what constitutes an easy‑to‑use interface.

claims.subject: real-time voice analysis
claims.explanation: The plan includes requirement R1 which mandates continuous analysis of the live microphone signal when the user starts, fulfilling the request for real‑time voice analysis.

claims.subject: basic pitch information
claims.explanation: Requirement R2 specifies showing the fundamental frequency, nearest note, and cents deviation, delivering the requested basic pitch data.

claims.subject: spectrogram display
claims.explanation: Requirement R4 provides a live scrolling spectrogram, satisfying the request for more complex information like a spectrogram.

claims.subject: pitch trace (singing trainer style)
claims.explanation: Requirement R3 adds a scrolling pitch trace over the last 8 seconds, a common feature of singing trainer apps.

claims.subject: formant estimation and vowel chart
claims.explanation: Requirement R6 estimates the first two formants and plots them on a vowel chart, mirroring features of accent‑training applications.

claims.subject: voice‑quality measures (jitter, shimmer, HNR)
claims.explanation: Requirement R7 reports jitter, shimmer and harmonics‑to‑noise ratio, which are typical voice‑quality metrics used in speech‑training tools.

claims.subject: vibrato detection
claims.explanation: Requirement R8 detects vibrato rate and extent, a feature commonly found in singing trainer apps.

claims.subject: plain‑language explanations for each measure
claims.explanation: Requirement R10 mandates that every displayed measure be explained in plain language, fulfilling the request to “tell me about it.”

claims.subject: easy‑to‑use single Start/Stop UI
claims.explanation: Requirement R12 specifies a desktop‑browser app with a single Start/Stop button as the only control, addressing the request for ease of use.

claims.subject: take inspiration from existing singing or accent trainer apps
claims.pointer: request:"take inspiration from existing singing or accent trainer apps"
claims.explanation: The request leaves the choice of which trainer‑style features to include open; the plan selected a specific set (pitch trace, formants, vowel chart, voice‑quality, vibrato). Human confirmation is needed that this selection matches the intended inspiration.

claims.subject: I want it to be easy to use
claims.pointer: request:"I want it to be easy to use"
claims.explanation: The request does not define what “easy to use” means; the plan chose a minimal UI with a single button and simple panels, which is a design decision requiring confirmation.
